text:
jordan_acme: hey team — our app just hit zero credits mid-demo. UI showed ~1200 left at 23:58 but by 00:02 API started returning 429s and then UI jumped to 0. we didn't change plans. any idea why this would happen? :grimacing:

mia_support: hi @jordan_acme — sorry about that. can you paste the tenant/org id and a short snippet of the request pattern? are these streaming calls or batch generation?

jordan_acme: tenant: acme-prod-42. pattern is a mix — lots of short chat completions (avg 40 tokens) + a few long streaming responses. we also saw a retry loop after a dependency timeout — logs show many rapid retries for ~3 minutes. here's a trimmed log showing counts: 
```
REQUEST_SUMMARY: 23:55 - 00:05 -> total_requests=11840, successful=11690, 429=150
RETRY_WINDOW: repeated retries peaked 23:58-00:01 (approx 900 retry attempts)
ERROR_SNIPPET: 429 {"error":"quota_exceeded","code":"quota_exhausted"}
```

mia_support: thanks. that helps. two quick clarifications: (1) what's the billing cycle reset timezone for this tenant? (2) did you see a `Retry-After` header on the 429 responses?

jordan_acme: billing cycle shows monthly reset at midnight in our org settings (we're on a monthly plan). UI showed "resets in 00:01:23" just before the zero. 429s included `Retry-After: 30` a few times but most were plain 429s.

mia_support: copying in @sam_oncall for enforcement/cache details. sam — can you check enforcement cache state for acme-prod-42 and whether any billing write lag was happening around midnight?

sam_oncall: looking now. I can see a short spike in enforcement writes at 00:00:15 UTC — billing service committed the new allowance at 00:00:15 but the enforcement cache on several edge nodes had stale entries until ~00:01:45 due to a propagation delay during the rollout. that means the UI (which reads the billing DB via a different path) showed the refreshed balance earlier, while the runtime enforcement layer was still counting down the old window and returning 429s.

jordan_acme: ah ok that explains UI vs API mismatch. but why were retries able to push us to zero if the reset happened? shouldn't the reset at midnight have restored tokens mid-retry window?

sam_oncall: two causes: (1) retries are counted as normal requests by the enforcement layer — if your client retried many times quickly those are additional token consumption. (2) we have a short grace window where cached allocation is conservative until the new balance is fully propagated to all workers; during high request density that can still exhaust the pre-reset allowance on the worker you hit.

lina_billing: to add — billing shows a full monthly refill record at 00:00:15 for acme-prod-42. we can issue a one-off top-up if you want immediate extra credits while you harden retries.

jordan_acme: appreciate that. what's the recommended client-side fix? we had exponential backoff but maybe our jitter was low.

mia_support: recommended pattern: respect `Retry-After` when provided, use capped exponential backoff with randomized jitter, and implement idempotency for actions that can be retried safely. example pseudo-curl + backoff: 
```
# when you get 429, check Retry-After header
# simple backoff pattern (js-like pseudocode)
wait = random_between(200,500)ms
attempt = 0
while (attempt < 5) {
  attempt++
  resp = send_request()
  if (resp.status != 429) break
  ra = resp.headers['Retry-After'] || min(1000 * 2**attempt, 10000)
  sleep(ra + random_between(0,200))
}
```

mia_support: also consider client-side rate limiting (leaky-bucket) to smooth bursts, and server-side batching if many small requests. if you need production-level protection against short spikes consider Dedicated capacity.

sam_oncall: operationally, I cleared the enforcement cache on the affected edge nodes at 00:01:50 which removed the stale zero state. you should see normal behavior now. we will follow up with an incident note describing the propagation lag and a mitigation (shorten enforcement TTL during rollouts).

quota-bot: ALERT: tenant acme-prod-42 enforcement cache cleared by sam_oncall at 1743220010. change-id: clear-cache-8312

jordan_acme: confirmed — calls are succeeding again, thanks. any ETA on the rollout-change to avoid this in future?

sam_oncall: we'll schedule a change this week to reduce TTL and add a faster fanout on billing commits. i'll file a follow-up postmortem.

lina_billing: i've also created a temporary credit top-up offer — if you want it applied while you tighten retries we can do that.

jordan_acme: please apply the top-up and send steps to avoid this on our side. thanks :raised_hands:

mia_support: noted — we'll apply a small emergency top-up and send a short best-practices checklist for retry/backoff and idempotency. closing loop once billing confirms.
